The main takeaway from our work is that

the low-frequency spin excitations in plane copper oxides are dominated by the interplay of two different types of charge carriers, namely, localized spins (holes) and weakly coupled itinerant charge carries (holes and electrons).
the nuclear spin relaxation is governed by the spin fluctuations of the itinerant carriers and not by localized spins as is commonly believed.
the nuclear relaxation rates are not only sensitive to the low-temperature spin dynamics, but also to the crossover between localized and weak coupling spin dynamics.
